models.name: erp_hrm_project_members
models.description: Links organization members to projects with role designation, enabling project team composition. Each record represents an employee's assignment to a project with their specific role within that project context. Project member roles are independent of organization-level roles.

models.name: erp_hrm_tasks
models.description: Work items representing units of work within projects. Tasks support a status workflow (Open, In-Progress, Completed, Closed), priority classification (Low, Medium, High, Critical), assignment to organization members, and single-level parent-child hierarchy for basic work breakdown structures. Each task belongs to a {@link erp_hrm_projects} and can optionally reference a parent task for sub-task relationships. Task assignment is optional via {@link erp_hrm_organization_members}. Tasks serve as the primary work tracking entity that timelogs are recorded against.

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged project's {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}. The project this task belongs to.

foreignFields.name: assigned_to_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned member's {@link erp_hrm_organization_members.id}. The organization member responsible for completing this task. Null if unassigned.

foreignFields.name: parent_task_id
foreignFields.description: Parent task's {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}. For sub-tasks, references the parent task. Limited to single-level nesting - child tasks cannot have their own children. Null for top-level tasks.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Task title or name. Brief summary of the work to be performed.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the task. May include requirements, acceptance criteria, or additional context.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the task. Allowed values: 'Open', 'In-Progress', 'Completed', 'Closed'. Open indicates ready to start, In-Progress indicates actively being worked, Completed indicates finished but not yet closed, Closed indicates archived or no longer active.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Priority level of the task. Allowed values: 'Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Critical'. Determines relative importance and urgency for work planning.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional deadline for task completion. When specified, indicates when the task should be finished.

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description: Optional estimated effort in hours required to complete the task. Used for planning and capacity management.

plainFields.name: created_at

models.name: erp_hrm_task_histories
models.description: Immutable audit trail recording status changes for tasks. Captures the complete history of task state transitions including previous and new status values, the user who performed the change, optional reason for the change, and precise timestamp. This append-only table ensures full accountability and compliance for task workflow tracking. References {@link erp_hrm_tasks} as the subject task and {@link erp_hrm_members} as the user who made the change.

foreignFields.name: erp_hrm_task_id

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: Task status after the change occurred (e.g., 'open', 'in_progress', 'completed').

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation or reason for the status change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the status change was recorded.

models.name: erp_hrm_timelogs
models.description: Individual time entries recording work sessions performed by employees. Each timelog represents a discrete unit of tracked time with start and end timestamps, duration calculated in minutes, project and optional task associations, and billable status classification. Timelogs form the foundational data for time tracking, payroll calculations, and project cost analysis. They can be aggregated into weekly timesheets for approval workflows. Timelogs have lifecycle constraints based on timesheet association - those not included in approved timesheets remain editable by their creators or users with time management permissions, while approved timelogs are permanently locked for audit integrity.

foreignFields.name: organization_member_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who created this timelog. {@link erp_hrm_organization_members.id}

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Project this time was logged against. {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional task within the project that this time was logged against. {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}

foreignFields.name: timesheet_id
foreignFields.description: Optional timesheet this timelog is included in. Null when timelog is independent. {@link erp_hrm_timesheets.id}

plainFields.name: start_time
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the work session began.

plainFields.name: end_time
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the work session ended.

plainFields.name: duration_minutes
plainFields.description: Duration of the work session in minutes, rounded to the nearest minute. Calculated from start_time and end_time.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description: Whether this time entry is billable to clients or internal. True for billable hours chargeable to clients, false for non-billable internal work.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description documenting what work was performed during this time entry.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion. Null if the timelog is active.

models.name: erp_hrm_timesheets
models.description:
Weekly collections of timelogs belonging to organization members with a complete approval workflow lifecycle. Timesheets aggregate all work hours recorded by an employee during a specific week, enabling structured review and approval processes.

The timesheet progresses through a status lifecycle: draft (initial collection of timelogs), submitted (awaiting review), approved (accepted and locked), or rejected (returned for correction). Once approved, all associated timelogs are locked to preserve the historical record.

Timesheets belong to a specific organization member and capture the week boundaries (start and end dates). When reviewed, the system records the reviewing organization member, review timestamp, and optional rejection reason to provide complete audit trail of the approval process.

{@link erp_hrm_organization_members} - The employee who owns this timesheet
{@link erp_hrm_organization_members} - The organization member who reviewed/approved the timesheet
{@link erp_hrm_timelogs} - Time entries included in this timesheet

foreignFields.name: organization_member_id
foreignFields.description: The organization member (employee) who owns this timesheet. {@link erp_hrm_organization_members.id}

foreignFields.name: reviewed_by_id
foreignFields.description: The organization member who reviewed and approved or rejected this timesheet. {@link erp_hrm_organization_members.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the timesheet in the approval workflow. Values: 'draft' (collecting timelogs), 'submitted' (awaiting review), 'approved' (accepted and locked), 'rejected' (returned for correction).

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description: Start date of the week covered by this timesheet (inclusive). Typically Sunday or Monday based on organization settings.

plainFields.name: week_end_date
plainFields.description: End date of the week covered by this timesheet (inclusive).

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was submitted for approval. Null while in draft status.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was reviewed (approved or rejected). Null until review occurs.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Explanation provided when a timesheet is rejected. Null for approved timesheets or when not yet reviewed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this timesheet record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if the timesheet is active, set when soft deleted for data retention.

models.name: erp_hrm_timers
models.description:
Active real-time tracking sessions for in-progress work that convert to timelogs when stopped.

Timers provide live time tracking capabilities, allowing employees to capture work duration as it occurs rather than estimating after completion. Each timer records the exact moment tracking began and associates the session with a project and optionally a specific task. When stopped, the timer automatically calculates the elapsed duration and creates a timelog entry containing the project, task, description, and calculated duration.

An employee can have at most one active timer at any moment. Timers persist indefinitely until explicitly stopped, accommodating various work patterns including long sessions. The timer serves as temporary state that gets converted to permanent timelog records upon completion.

foreignFields.name: organization_member_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who owns this timer. {@link erp_hrm_organization_members.id}

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Project being worked on during this timer session. {@link erp_hrm_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional specific task being worked on. {@link erp_hrm_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of the work being performed during this timer session.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer began tracking. Used to calculate duration when converting to timelog.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

models.name: erp_hrm_activity_logs
models.description: Audit trail logging all significant actions performed by users within an organization. Records who performed what action, when, and on which entity. Supports compliance and security auditing requirements.

foreignFields.name: actor_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest who performed the action's {@link erp_hrm_guests.id}. Nullable when action performed by member.

plainFields.name: action

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: The type of entity affected by the action (e.g., 'member', 'department', 'project', 'task').

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: The UUID of the specific entity affected by the action.

plainFields.name: ip_address

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the client that performed the action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the log entry was created.

models.name: erp_hrm_activity_log_details
models.description: Normalized key-value pairs storing detailed metadata for activity log entries. Supports flexible schema for different action types while maintaining 1NF compliance by decomposing variable action details into atomic key-value records rather than storing JSON. Common metadata includes before/after values for status changes, rejection reasons for timesheet reviews, and other contextual data that reconstructs full circumstances of recorded actions.

foreignFields.name: activity_log_id
foreignFields.description: Parent activity log entry. {@link erp_hrm_activity_logs.id}

plainFields.name: key

plainFields.name: value

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this detail record was created.

### `erp_hrm_guests`

Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors before
registration. Guests are identified by device fingerprint and have
limited access to pre-authentication features. Guest accounts are
temporary and expire after a set duration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `device_fingerprint`
  > Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest's device/browser. Used to
  > recognize returning guests before registration.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account expires. Used for automatic cleanup of
  > stale guest accounts.

### `erp_hrm_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access to pre-authentication features.
Guest sessions allow unauthenticated visitors to interact with the system
before registration. Each session tracks connection metadata (IP,
referrer) and has an expiration for security. Sessions are append-only
audit records of guest access.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `guest_id`: Belonged guest's [erp_hrm_guests.id](#erp_hrm_guests).
- `ip`: Client IP address at session creation.
- `href`: URL where the guest session was initiated.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL indicating the source of the guest session.
- `created_at`: Creation time of the session.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration time. After this time, the session is no longer valid.

### `erp_hrm_members`

Global member identity representing registered users with email/password
credentials. This is the canonical identity record that spans across all
organizations - a single user account can belong to multiple
organizations via [erp_hrm_organization_members](#erp_hrm_organization_members). Contains
authentication credentials and profile information.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be
  > valid email format.
- `password_hash`
  > Bcrypt hashed password for authentication. Never store plain text
  > passwords.
- `first_name`: Member's first name for profile display.
- `last_name`: Member's last name for profile display.
- `avatar_url`: Optional URL to member's profile avatar image.
- `timezone`
  > Member's preferred timezone for displaying dates and times. Defaults to
  > organization timezone if not set.
- `locale`
  > Member's preferred language locale (e.g., 'en-US', 'ko-KR') for localized
  > content.
- `email_verified_at`: Timestamp when email was verified. Null if not yet verified.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null if account is active.

### `erp_hrm_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for authenticated member sessions. Tracks active login
sessions with access tokens, refresh tokens, and connection metadata (IP,
referrer). Each session belongs to a member and expires after a defined
period for security. Sessions are append-only audit records of member
authentication events.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `erp_hrm_member_id`: Belonged member's [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members).
- `access_token`: JWT access token for API authentication.
- `refresh_token`: JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.
- `ip`: Client IP address from which the session was initiated.
- `href`: URL or endpoint where the authentication request originated.
- `referrer`: HTTP referrer header indicating the source of the authentication request.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expires. Used for security to limit session
  > lifetime.

### `erp_hrm_member_password_resets`

Temporary password reset tokens for member account recovery.

Each record represents a single password reset request initiated by a
member. The system generates a unique token that is delivered to the
member's registered email address. The token has a limited validity
period defined by expires_at. Once used successfully, the consumed_at
timestamp is set to prevent replay attacks.

Password reset tokens are single-use and expire automatically after a
configured time period (typically 24 hours). Members can request multiple
reset tokens, but only the most recent unexpired token is valid for use.
This table maintains an audit trail of all password reset attempts for
security monitoring purposes.

[erp_hrm_members](#erp_hrm_members)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `erp_hrm_member_id`
  > Belonged member's [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members). The member who requested
  > the password reset.
- `token`
  > Unique cryptographically secure random token sent to the member's email
  > for password reset verification. Must be unpredictable and single-use.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when the reset token becomes invalid. Tokens past this datetime
  > cannot be used for password reset regardless of consumption status.
- `consumed_at`
  > Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset the password.
  > Once consumed, the token is permanently invalidated to prevent replay
  > attacks. Null if not yet consumed.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the password reset was requested and this record was
  > created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the last update to this record. Typically set when the token
  > is consumed.

### `erp_hrm_member_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for member registration confirmation.

Stores verification tokens sent to users during the registration process
to confirm ownership of their email address. Each token is time-limited
for security purposes and becomes invalid after expiration or upon
successful verification.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `erp_hrm_member_id`: The member account awaiting email verification. [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members)
- `token`
  > Cryptographically secure verification token sent to the user's email
  > address. Must be unique and unpredictable.
- `email`
  > The email address being verified. Stored to ensure the verified email
  > matches the token recipient.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when the verification token becomes invalid. Tokens are
  > typically valid for a limited time (e.g., 24 hours) for security.
- `verified_at`
  > Timestamp when the email was successfully verified. Null until
  > verification is completed.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the verification token was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the verification record was last modified.

### `erp_hrm_organizations`

Root tenant entity representing companies/organizations in the erpHrm
system.

This table serves as the aggregate root for all organization-scoped data
isolation. Each organization contains identity information (name,
description, logo) and configuration settings (currency, timezone, fiscal
calendar) that define how the organization operates within the system.

Organizations are owned by a User (referenced via owner_id) who has
administrative control. All other domain entities (members, roles,
departments, projects, tasks, etc.) belong to an organization and are
isolated from other organizations.

Soft deletion is supported via deleted_at to allow for data recovery and
maintain referential integrity with historical records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `owner_id`
  > Owner user's [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members). The user who created and owns
  > this organization.
- `name`: Organization name. Display name for the company/organization.
- `description`
  > Optional organization description. Brief summary of the organization's
  > purpose or business.
- `logo_url`: Optional URL to the organization's logo image.
- `currency`
  > Default currency for the organization in ISO 4217 format (e.g., USD, EUR,
  > KRW). Used for financial calculations and reporting.
- `timezone`
  > Organization's default timezone in IANA format (e.g., America/New_York,
  > Asia/Seoul). Used for datetime localization.
- `fiscal_year_start_month`
  > Month when the fiscal year starts (1-12). Used for financial reporting
  > and analytics.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the organization was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the organization was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null if active, set when organization is deleted.

### `erp_hrm_organization_members`

Employee records linking global users to specific organizations. Each
record represents a membership that connects a user account to an
organizational context, enabling the user to perform work within that
organization. Contains role assignment for access control, optional
department placement for organizational structure, position/title for
hierarchy identification, employment type classification, and activation
status for lifecycle management. Serves as the bridge entity that makes
all work data (timelogs, timesheets, project assignments)
organization-scoped.

Key business relationships:
- Belongs to [erp_hrm_organizations](#erp_hrm_organizations) via organization_id
- Links to global [erp_hrm_members](#erp_hrm_members) via user_id
- Assigned [erp_hrm_roles](#erp_hrm_roles) for permissions
- Optionally belongs to [erp_hrm_departments](#erp_hrm_departments)
- Has many [erp_hrm_contracts](#erp_hrm_contracts), [erp_hrm_project_members](#erp_hrm_project_members),
[erp_hrm_timelogs](#erp_hrm_timelogs), [erp_hrm_timesheets](#erp_hrm_timesheets), {@link
erp_hrm_timers}

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`: Belonged organization's [erp_hrm_organizations.id](#erp_hrm_organizations).
- `user_id`: Linked global user's [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members).
- `role_id`: Assigned role's [erp_hrm_roles.id](#erp_hrm_roles) determining permissions.
- `department_id`: Optional department assignment's [erp_hrm_departments.id](#erp_hrm_departments).
- `position`
  > Optional job title or position within the organization (e.g., 'Senior
  > Developer', 'Project Manager').
- `employment_type`
  > Classification of working relationship: 'full_time', 'part_time',
  > 'contractor', or 'intern'.
- `is_active`
  > Activation status indicating whether the member can perform work
  > activities. true=active, false=deactivated.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the membership was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last membership update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for preserving historical work records.

### `erp_hrm_roles`

Permission sets defined within an organization. Includes built-in roles
(Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom roles with configurable
permissions. Assigned to organization members to control access rights.
Each role belongs to exactly one organization and role names must be
unique within that organization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`: Belonged organization's [erp_hrm_organizations.id](#erp_hrm_organizations).
- `name`: Role name (e.g., Owner, Manager, Employee, or custom role name).
- `description`: Optional description of the role's purpose and responsibilities.
- `is_builtin`
  > Whether this is a system-defined built-in role (Owner, Manager, Employee)
  > or a custom user-defined role.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null if role is active.

### `erp_hrm_departments`

Organizational hierarchy structure representing functional divisions or
departments within a company.

Departments provide the organizational structure needed to categorize
employees and reflect the company's internal hierarchy. Each department
belongs to exactly one organization and can optionally have a parent
department, supporting single-level parent-child nesting for department
trees.

Departments are used for employee classification, organizational
reporting, and filtering employee lists. Employees may be optionally
assigned to a single department within their organization, reflecting
their placement within the organizational structure.

The department hierarchy enables organizational chart visualization and
department-based grouping for management and reporting purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`: Belonged organization's [erp_hrm_organizations.id](#erp_hrm_organizations).
- `parent_department_id`
  > Parent department's [erp_hrm_departments.id](#erp_hrm_departments) for hierarchical

- `name`: Department name (e.g., 'Engineering', 'Sales', 'Human Resources').
- `description`
  > Optional description providing additional context about the department's
  > purpose and responsibilities.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null if department is active.

### `erp_hrm_contracts`

Employment contract records for organization members. Tracks formal
employment agreements including compensation terms, working hours, and
employment periods. Maintains complete historical record of all contracts
with only one active contract per member at any time. Supports payroll
processing, labor cost calculations, and compliance audit trails.

Properties as follows:

- `organization_member_id`: Belonged organization member's [erp_hrm_organization_members.id](#erp_hrm_organization_members).

### `erp_hrm_projects`

Work initiatives within an organization that serve as containers for
tasks and time tracking.

Projects represent organizational work efforts with defined scope,
timelines, and team assignments. Each project belongs to a single
organization and can have multiple members assigned through {@link
erp_hrm_project_members}. Projects contain tasks ([erp_hrm_tasks](#erp_hrm_tasks))
and accumulate time entries ([erp_hrm_timelogs](#erp_hrm_timelogs)) from assigned
members.

Projects progress through a lifecycle status: active (receiving new
work), archived (temporarily inactive), and completed (finished). Only
active projects can receive new timelogs. Archived projects may be
reactivated, while completed projects represent final closure.

Planning attributes include budget hours for capacity planning and
optional start/end dates for scheduling. The color code provides visual
identification in user interfaces.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`: Belongs to [erp_hrm_organizations.id](#erp_hrm_organizations).
- `name`: Project name identifying the work initiative.
- `color_code`: Hex color code for visual identification in UI.
- `description`: Detailed description of project scope and objectives.
- `status`: Lifecycle status: active, archived, or completed.
- `budget_hours`: Planned budget hours for capacity planning.
- `start_date`: Scheduled project start date.
- `end_date`: Scheduled project end date.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the project was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the project was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if active.

- `project_id`: Belonged project's [erp_hrm_projects.id](#erp_hrm_projects).
- `organization_member_id`: Assigned organization member's [erp_hrm_organization_members.id](#erp_hrm_organization_members).
- `role`

  > participation rights) or 'project-lead' (task management authority within
  > the project).
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if record is active.

Work items representing units of work within projects. Tasks support a
status workflow (Open, In-Progress, Completed, Closed), priority
classification (Low, Medium, High, Critical), assignment to organization
members, and single-level parent-child hierarchy for basic work breakdown
structures. Each task belongs to a [erp_hrm_projects](#erp_hrm_projects) and can
optionally reference a parent task for sub-task relationships. Task
assignment is optional via [erp_hrm_organization_members](#erp_hrm_organization_members). Tasks
serve as the primary work tracking entity that timelogs are recorded
against.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `project_id`
  > Belonged project's [erp_hrm_projects.id](#erp_hrm_projects). The project this task
  > belongs to.
- `assigned_to_id`
  > Assigned member's [erp_hrm_organization_members.id](#erp_hrm_organization_members). The
  > organization member responsible for completing this task. Null if
  > unassigned.
- `parent_task_id`
  > Parent task's [erp_hrm_tasks.id](#erp_hrm_tasks). For sub-tasks, references the
  > parent task. Limited to single-level nesting - child tasks cannot have
  > their own children. Null for top-level tasks.
- `title`: Task title or name. Brief summary of the work to be performed.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the task. May include requirements, acceptance
  > criteria, or additional context.
- `status`
  > Current status of the task. Allowed values: 'Open', 'In-Progress',
  > 'Completed', 'Closed'. Open indicates ready to start, In-Progress
  > indicates actively being worked, Completed indicates finished but not yet
  > closed, Closed indicates archived or no longer active.
- `priority`
  > Priority level of the task. Allowed values: 'Low', 'Medium', 'High',
  > 'Critical'. Determines relative importance and urgency for work planning.
- `due_date`
  > Optional deadline for task completion. When specified, indicates when the
  > task should be finished.
- `estimated_hours`
  > Optional estimated effort in hours required to complete the task. Used
  > for planning and capacity management.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the task was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the task was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp for soft delete. Null if task is active, set when task is
  > deleted.

### `erp_hrm_task_histories`

Immutable audit trail recording status changes for tasks. Captures the
complete history of task state transitions including previous and new
status values, the user who performed the change, optional reason for the
change, and precise timestamp. This append-only table ensures full
accountability and compliance for task workflow tracking. References
[erp_hrm_tasks](#erp_hrm_tasks) as the subject task and [erp_hrm_members](#erp_hrm_members) as
the user who made the change.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `erp_hrm_task_id`: Target task's [erp_hrm_tasks.id](#erp_hrm_tasks).
- `erp_hrm_member_id`: Member who performed the change's [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members).
- `previous_status`
  > Task status before the change occurred (e.g., 'open', 'in_progress',
  > 'completed').
- `new_status`
  > Task status after the change occurred (e.g., 'open', 'in_progress',
  > 'completed').
- `change_reason`: Optional explanation or reason for the status change.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the status change was recorded.

### `erp_hrm_timelogs`

Individual time entries recording work sessions performed by employees.
Each timelog represents a discrete unit of tracked time with start and
end timestamps, duration calculated in minutes, project and optional task
associations, and billable status classification. Timelogs form the
foundational data for time tracking, payroll calculations, and project
cost analysis. They can be aggregated into weekly timesheets for approval
workflows. Timelogs have lifecycle constraints based on timesheet
association - those not included in approved timesheets remain editable
by their creators or users with time management permissions, while
approved timelogs are permanently locked for audit integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_member_id`: Employee who created this timelog. [erp_hrm_organization_members.id](#erp_hrm_organization_members)
- `project_id`: Project this time was logged against. [erp_hrm_projects.id](#erp_hrm_projects)
- `task_id`
  > Optional task within the project that this time was logged against.
  > [erp_hrm_tasks.id](#erp_hrm_tasks)
- `timesheet_id`
  > Optional timesheet this timelog is included in. Null when timelog is
  > independent. [erp_hrm_timesheets.id](#erp_hrm_timesheets)
- `start_time`: Timestamp when the work session began.
- `end_time`: Timestamp when the work session ended.
- `duration_minutes`
  > Duration of the work session in minutes, rounded to the nearest minute.
  > Calculated from start_time and end_time.
- `billable`
  > Whether this time entry is billable to clients or internal. True for
  > billable hours chargeable to clients, false for non-billable internal
  > work.
- `description`
  > Optional description documenting what work was performed during this time
  > entry.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the timelog was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the timelog was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion. Null if the timelog is active.

### `erp_hrm_timesheets`

Weekly collections of timelogs belonging to organization members with a
complete approval workflow lifecycle. Timesheets aggregate all work hours
recorded by an employee during a specific week, enabling structured
review and approval processes.

The timesheet progresses through a status lifecycle: draft (initial
collection of timelogs), submitted (awaiting review), approved (accepted
and locked), or rejected (returned for correction). Once approved, all
associated timelogs are locked to preserve the historical record.

Timesheets belong to a specific organization member and capture the week
boundaries (start and end dates). When reviewed, the system records the
reviewing organization member, review timestamp, and optional rejection
reason to provide complete audit trail of the approval process.

[erp_hrm_organization_members](#erp_hrm_organization_members) - The employee who owns this timesheet
[erp_hrm_organization_members](#erp_hrm_organization_members) - The organization member who
reviewed/approved the timesheet
[erp_hrm_timelogs](#erp_hrm_timelogs) - Time entries included in this timesheet

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_member_id`
  > The organization member (employee) who owns this timesheet. {@link
  > erp_hrm_organization_members.id}
- `reviewed_by_id`
  > The organization member who reviewed and approved or rejected this
  > timesheet. [erp_hrm_organization_members.id](#erp_hrm_organization_members)
- `status`
  > Current status of the timesheet in the approval workflow. Values: 'draft'
  > (collecting timelogs), 'submitted' (awaiting review), 'approved'
  > (accepted and locked), 'rejected' (returned for correction).
- `week_start_date`
  > Start date of the week covered by this timesheet (inclusive). Typically
  > Sunday or Monday based on organization settings.
- `week_end_date`: End date of the week covered by this timesheet (inclusive).
- `submitted_at`
  > Timestamp when the timesheet was submitted for approval. Null while in
  > draft status.
- `reviewed_at`
  > Timestamp when the timesheet was reviewed (approved or rejected). Null
  > until review occurs.
- `rejection_reason`
  > Explanation provided when a timesheet is rejected. Null for approved
  > timesheets or when not yet reviewed.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the timesheet record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to this timesheet record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. Null if the timesheet is active, set when soft
  > deleted for data retention.

### `erp_hrm_timers`

Active real-time tracking sessions for in-progress work that convert to
timelogs when stopped.

Timers provide live time tracking capabilities, allowing employees to
capture work duration as it occurs rather than estimating after
completion. Each timer records the exact moment tracking began and
associates the session with a project and optionally a specific task.
When stopped, the timer automatically calculates the elapsed duration and
creates a timelog entry containing the project, task, description, and
calculated duration.

An employee can have at most one active timer at any moment. Timers
persist indefinitely until explicitly stopped, accommodating various work
patterns including long sessions. The timer serves as temporary state
that gets converted to permanent timelog records upon completion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_member_id`: Employee who owns this timer. [erp_hrm_organization_members.id](#erp_hrm_organization_members)
- `project_id`
  > Project being worked on during this timer session. {@link
  > erp_hrm_projects.id}
- `task_id`: Optional specific task being worked on. [erp_hrm_tasks.id](#erp_hrm_tasks)
- `description`: Description of the work being performed during this timer session.
- `started_at`
  > Timestamp when the timer began tracking. Used to calculate duration when
  > converting to timelog.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.

### `erp_hrm_activity_logs`

Audit trail logging all significant actions performed by users within an
organization. Records who performed what action, when, and on which
entity. Supports compliance and security auditing requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `organization_id`: Belonged organization's [erp_hrm_organizations.id](#erp_hrm_organizations).
- `actor_member_id`
  > Member who performed the action's [erp_hrm_members.id](#erp_hrm_members). Nullable
  > when action performed by system or guest.
- `actor_guest_id`
  > Guest who performed the action's [erp_hrm_guests.id](#erp_hrm_guests). Nullable when
  > action performed by member.
- `action`
  > The type of action performed (e.g., 'create', 'update', 'delete',
  > 'login', 'logout').
- `entity_type`
  > The type of entity affected by the action (e.g., 'member', 'department',
  > 'project', 'task').
- `entity_id`: The UUID of the specific entity affected by the action.
- `ip_address`: IP address from which the action was performed.
- `user_agent`: User agent string of the client that performed the action.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the log entry was created.

### `erp_hrm_activity_log_details`

Normalized key-value pairs storing detailed metadata for activity log
entries. Supports flexible schema for different action types while
maintaining 1NF compliance by decomposing variable action details into
atomic key-value records rather than storing JSON. Common metadata
includes before/after values for status changes, rejection reasons for
timesheet reviews, and other contextual data that reconstructs full
circumstances of recorded actions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `activity_log_id`: Parent activity log entry. [erp_hrm_activity_logs.id](#erp_hrm_activity_logs)
- `key`
  > Metadata key identifying the type of detail being stored (e.g.,
  > 'previous_status', 'new_status', 'rejection_reason', 'before_value',
  > 'after_value').
- `value`
  > Metadata value associated with the key. Stores the actual contextual data
  > such as status values, rejection reasons, or before/after states.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this detail record was created.

operations.specification: Service implementation: Validate the device fingerprint from request. Create or find existing guest record by device fingerprint. Generate new guest session with JWT access and refresh tokens. Store session in erp_hrm_guest_sessions with IP, href, referrer tracking. Set expiration based on schema's expired_at pattern. Return tokens in IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized format.
operations.description:
Initialize guest access by creating a guest account identified by device fingerprint.

This endpoint creates a temporary guest session for unauthenticated visitors. The device fingerprint uniquely identifies the visitor's browser/device. Upon successful creation, a guest record is established in erp_hrm_guests and a session is created in erp_hrm_guest_sessions with generated JWT tokens.

The session includes access and refresh tokens for subsequent API calls. Client metadata (IP address, current href, referrer) is captured for audit purposes. The session has an expiration time after which it becomes invalid.

No authentication is required - this is a public endpoint for first-time visitors.

requestBody.description: Guest initialization request with device fingerprint and client metadata

responseBody.description: Guest authentication response containing access and refresh tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Service implementation: Validate the provided refresh token. Look up existing guest session in erp_hrm_guest_sessions. Verify session is not expired (check expired_at field). Generate new access token with extended expiration. Update session record with new token values and refresh expiration. Return updated IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized tokens.
operations.description:
Extend guest session validity by refreshing authentication tokens.

This endpoint allows an active guest session to obtain new access tokens before expiration. The existing refresh token is validated against the erp_hrm_guest_sessions table, checking that the session exists and has not expired (expired_at timestamp validation).

Upon successful validation, new tokens are generated with refreshed expiration times. The session record is updated with the new token information. This maintains continuous guest access without requiring re-initialization.

No actor authentication required - the refresh token itself provides sufficient verification for this public endpoint.

requestBody.description: Guest token refresh request containing the current refresh token

responseBody.description: Guest authentication response with refreshed access and refresh tokens

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email format and uniqueness against erp_hrm_members table; 2) Hash password using bcrypt with salt rounds; 3) Create member record with provided email, password_hash, first_name, last_name; 4) Generate email verification token and store in erp_hrm_member_email_verifications; 5) Send verification email; 6) Generate JWT access_token and refresh_token, store session in erp_hrm_member_sessions; 7) Return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized with tokens and member info.
operations.description:
Registers a new member account in the erpHrm system.

This operation creates a new member identity with email/password credentials. It validates that the email is unique and properly formatted, hashes the password securely using bcrypt, and creates the member record in the erp_hrm_members table. Upon successful registration, the system generates email verification tokens stored in erp_hrm_member_email_verifications table and creates a new authenticated session.

The registration flow includes: email validation, password strength verification, member record creation, session token generation, and email verification token issuance. The returned IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized contains both access_token for immediate API use and refresh_token for token renewal.

This is a public endpoint that requires no authentication. The authorizationActor is "member", indicating this operation is for the member actor type. After registration, members can proceed to log in and access organization features.

requestBody.description: Member registration credentials including email, password, first name, and last name.

responseBody.description: Newly created member with authentication tokens (access_token and refresh_token).

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Lookup member by email in erp_hrm_members table; 2) Verify bcrypt password hash matches; 3) Check if account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null); 4) Generate new JWT access_token and refresh_token; 5) Create session record in erp_hrm_member_sessions with ip, href, referrer metadata; 6) Return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized with tokens and member profile data.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing member with email and password credentials.

This operation validates member credentials by looking up the email in erp_hrm_members table and verifying the bcrypt password hash. It ensures the account is active (deleted_at is null). Upon successful authentication, a new session is created in erp_hrm_member_sessions table storing the JWT tokens along with connection metadata (IP address, referrer, href).

The login flow generates fresh access_token and refresh_token pair for the authenticated session. The access_token is used for subsequent API requests, while the refresh_token allows obtaining new access tokens when the current one expires without requiring re-authentication.

This is a public endpoint requiring no prior authentication. The authorizationActor is "member", indicating this operation is for the member actor type. Failed attempts should not reveal whether email or password was incorrect for security. The returned IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized includes complete member profile information along with the authentication tokens.

requestBody.description: Member login credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: Authenticated member with new access and refresh tokens.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate the provided refresh_token; 2) Lookup existing session in erp_hrm_member_sessions by refresh_token; 3) Verify session is not expired (compare expired_at with current time); 4) Generate new JWT access_token and refresh_token pair; 5) Update session record with new tokens; 6) Return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized with updated tokens and member info.
operations.description:
Refreshes an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

This operation allows extending authentication sessions without requiring the member to re-enter credentials. The refresh_token from the request is validated against the erp_hrm_member_sessions table to ensure it exists and has not expired (expired_at > current time). If valid, a new token pair is generated and the session record is updated.

Token refresh is essential for maintaining secure long-lived sessions. The access_token typically has a short lifetime (e.g., 15 minutes) while the refresh_token remains valid longer (e.g., 7 days). When the access_token expires, clients can call this endpoint to obtain fresh tokens.

The operation requires a valid refresh token but no active access token (authorizationType: refresh). The authorizationActor is "member", indicating this operation is for the member actor type. Invalid or expired refresh tokens result in authentication errors requiring the member to log in again. The returned IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized contains the new token pair with updated expiration times.

requestBody.description: Refresh token used to obtain new access token.

responseBody.description: Member with refreshed authentication tokens.

operations.description:
Initialize guest access by creating a guest account identified by device fingerprint.

This endpoint creates a temporary guest session for unauthenticated visitors. The device fingerprint uniquely identifies the visitor's browser/device. Upon successful creation, a guest record is established in erp_hrm_guests and a session is created in erp_hrm_guest_sessions with generated JWT tokens.

The session includes access and refresh tokens for subsequent API calls. Client metadata (IP address, current href, referrer) is captured for audit purposes. The session has an expiration time after which it becomes invalid.

No authentication is required - this is a public endpoint for first-time visitors.

requestBody.description: Guest initialization request with device fingerprint and client metadata

responseBody.description: Guest authentication response containing access and refresh tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Service implementation: Validate the provided refresh token. Look up existing guest session in erp_hrm_guest_sessions. Verify session is not expired (check expired_at field). Generate new access token with extended expiration. Update session record with new token values and refresh expiration. Return updated IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized tokens.
operations.description:
Extend guest session validity by refreshing authentication tokens.

This endpoint allows an active guest session to obtain new access tokens before expiration. The existing refresh token is validated against the erp_hrm_guest_sessions table, checking that the session exists and has not expired (expired_at timestamp validation).

Upon successful validation, new tokens are generated with refreshed expiration times. The session record is updated with the new token information. This maintains continuous guest access without requiring re-initialization.

No actor authentication required - the refresh token itself provides sufficient verification for this public endpoint.

requestBody.description: Guest token refresh request containing the current refresh token

responseBody.description: Guest authentication response with refreshed access and refresh tokens

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email format and uniqueness against erp_hrm_members table; 2) Hash password using bcrypt with salt rounds; 3) Create member record with provided email, password_hash, first_name, last_name; 4) Generate email verification token and store in erp_hrm_member_email_verifications; 5) Send verification email; 6) Generate JWT access_token and refresh_token, store session in erp_hrm_member_sessions; 7) Return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized with tokens and member info.
operations.description:
Registers a new member account in the erpHrm system.

This operation creates a new member identity with email/password credentials. It validates that the email is unique and properly formatted, hashes the password securely using bcrypt, and creates the member record in the erp_hrm_members table. Upon successful registration, the system generates email verification tokens stored in erp_hrm_member_email_verifications table and creates a new authenticated session.

The registration flow includes: email validation, password strength verification, member record creation, session token generation, and email verification token issuance. The returned IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized contains both access_token for immediate API use and refresh_token for token renewal.

This is a public endpoint that requires no authentication. The authorizationActor is "member", indicating this operation is for the member actor type. After registration, members can proceed to log in and access organization features.

requestBody.description: Member registration credentials including email, password, first name, and last name.

responseBody.description: Newly created member with authentication tokens (access_token and refresh_token).

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Lookup member by email in erp_hrm_members table; 2) Verify bcrypt password hash matches; 3) Check if account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null); 4) Generate new JWT access_token and refresh_token; 5) Create session record in erp_hrm_member_sessions with ip, href, referrer metadata; 6) Return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized with tokens and member profile data.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing member with email and password credentials.

This operation validates member credentials by looking up the email in erp_hrm_members table and verifying the bcrypt password hash. It ensures the account is active (deleted_at is null). Upon successful authentication, a new session is created in erp_hrm_member_sessions table storing the JWT tokens along with connection metadata (IP address, referrer, href).

The login flow generates fresh access_token and refresh_token pair for the authenticated session. The access_token is used for subsequent API requests, while the refresh_token allows obtaining new access tokens when the current one expires without requiring re-authentication.

This is a public endpoint requiring no prior authentication. The authorizationActor is "member", indicating this operation is for the member actor type. Failed attempts should not reveal whether email or password was incorrect for security. The returned IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized includes complete member profile information along with the authentication tokens.

requestBody.description: Member login credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: Authenticated member with new access and refresh tokens.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate the provided refresh_token; 2) Lookup existing session in erp_hrm_member_sessions by refresh_token; 3) Verify session is not expired (compare expired_at with current time); 4) Generate new JWT access_token and refresh_token pair; 5) Update session record with new tokens; 6) Return IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized with updated tokens and member info.
operations.description:
Refreshes an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

This operation allows extending authentication sessions without requiring the member to re-enter credentials. The refresh_token from the request is validated against the erp_hrm_member_sessions table to ensure it exists and has not expired (expired_at > current time). If valid, a new token pair is generated and the session record is updated.

Token refresh is essential for maintaining secure long-lived sessions. The access_token typically has a short lifetime (e.g., 15 minutes) while the refresh_token remains valid longer (e.g., 7 days). When the access_token expires, clients can call this endpoint to obtain fresh tokens.

The operation requires a valid refresh token but no active access token (authorizationType: refresh). The authorizationActor is "member", indicating this operation is for the member actor type. Invalid or expired refresh tokens result in authentication errors requiring the member to log in again. The returned IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized contains the new token pair with updated expiration times.

requestBody.description: Refresh token used to obtain new access token.

responseBody.description: Member with refreshed authentication tokens.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organization members (employees).

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for browsing employees within the current organization context. Organization members represent the link between global user accounts and organizational membership, containing role assignments, department placements, employment classifications, and activation status.

Filtering capabilities include role-based filtering, department filtering, active/deactivated status filtering, and text search across member names and emails. The response includes essential summary information optimized for list displays, with joined data from user profiles (name, email, avatar), role definitions, and department assignments.

Access is restricted based on the requesting member's permissions. Members with employee viewing permissions can access all organization members, while standard members may have limited visibility based on organizational policies. Deactivated members remain in results for administrative purposes but are identifiable via the isActive flag.

Results are ordered by creation date (newest first) by default, with configurable sorting options. Pagination uses cursor-based strategies for optimal performance with large organizations. The operation respects the current organization context established in the authenticated session.

Related operations: POST /members for inviting new members, PUT /members/{memberId} for updating member details, GET /members/{memberId} for detailed member information.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_organization_members table with the following implementation details:

1. Organization Scope: Filter by the organization_id from the current session context (erp_hrm_member_sessions.organization_id).

2. Database Joins:
   - INNER JOIN erp_hrm_members ON organization_members.user_id = members.id (for user profile data: first_name, last_name, email, avatar_url)
   - INNER JOIN erp_hrm_roles ON organization_members.role_id = roles.id (for role name)
   - LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_departments ON organization_members.department_id = departments.id (for department name, handle null departments)

3. Soft Delete Filtering: Exclude records where organization_members.deleted_at IS NOT NULL (unless explicitly requested via includeDeleted flag in request).

4. Search Filters (applied when provided in request body):
   - roleIds: Filter by organization_members.role_id IN (provided UUIDs)
   - departmentIds: Filter by organization_members.department_id IN (provided UUIDs), include NULL when 'unassigned' sentinel provided
   - isActive: Filter by organization_members.is_active = true/false
   - searchText: Perform ILIKE search across members.first_name, members.last_name, members.email, and organization_members.position using OR conditions with Gin indexes
   - employmentType: Filter by organization_members.employment_type IN (provided values)

5. Sorting: Support sort by created_at (default DESC), first_name, last_name, role.name, department.name. Validate sort field against whitelist to prevent injection.

6. Pagination: Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at + id as cursor. Support configurable page size with max limit (100).

7. Permission Check: Verify requesting member has 'employee:read' or 'employee:manage' permission via their role assignment before executing query.

8. Response Projection: Select id, position, employment_type, is_active, created_at from organization_members; id, first_name, last_name, email, avatar_url from members; id, name from roles; id, name from departments.

9. Edge Cases:
   - Empty result: Return empty data array with valid pagination metadata
   - Invalid cursor: Return 400 with clear error message
   - Unauthorized: Return 403 if lacking permissions
   - Soft-deleted members: Exclude by default, include only with explicit permission and flag

10. Performance: Ensure proper index usage on organization_id, role_id, department_id, and deleted_at columns.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization member summaries with joined user, role, and department data

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering organization members

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of authenticated member's JWT sessions.

This operation allows members to audit their active and historical authentication sessions. Sessions contain JWT access tokens, refresh tokens, IP addresses, HTTP referrer information, creation timestamps, and expiration timestamps that together form a complete security audit trail.

The system provides search and filtering capabilities including date ranges for session creation and expiration, IP address patterns, and referrer URL patterns. This enables members to identify suspicious login activity, view sessions from specific devices or locations, and track authentication history over time.

Security considerations: The response includes session summaries with truncated or masked token representations - full token values are never returned in list operations. Sessions are append-only immutable records that cannot be modified by users, reflecting their role as security audit logs of authentication events.

Related operations: Access GET /sessions/{sessionId} to retrieve detailed information about a specific session, DELETE /sessions/{sessionId} to terminate a specific session (logout from that device), or POST /auth/logout to terminate all sessions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_member_sessions table filtered by the authenticated member's ID. Apply search filters on created_at date range (createdAfter, createdBefore), expired_at status (expired, active, or both), IP address pattern matching, and referrer URL pattern matching.

Return paginated results using cursor-based pagination for optimal performance with large session histories. Each session summary should include id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, and a flag indicating if the session is currently active (expired_at > now()).

Exclude sensitive data from the response: access_token and refresh_token should never be returned in full. Instead, return truncated representations (first/last few characters) or simply omit them from the summary view.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member session summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering sessions

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member authentication session.

This endpoint returns the complete session record identified by the sessionId path parameter. Sessions represent active login sessions and contain authentication tokens (access and refresh tokens) along with connection metadata such as the originating IP address, referrer URL, and creation/expiry timestamps.

The retrieved session information is scoped to the current organization context selected in the active session. Members can only access their own session information or sessions they have appropriate permissions to view based on their role within the organization.

This operation is typically used for session management purposes, such as viewing active sessions across devices, auditing authentication events, or checking session expiry status before token refresh operations.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_member_sessions table by primary key using the provided sessionId parameter from the URL path.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate sessionId is a valid UUID format
2. Query erp_hrm_member_sessions where id equals sessionId
3. Verify the session belongs to the requesting member or the user has administrative permissions to view member sessions
4. Return the session entity with all fields: id, access_token, refresh_token, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, erp_hrm_member_id
5. Apply organization context filtering - only return sessions that belong to the current organization context
6. Handle not found error when session does not exist or user lacks permission to view it
7. Consider performance by using the index on erp_hrm_member_id and created_at for validation queries

responseBody.description: The complete session object containing authentication tokens, connection metadata, and timestamps.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the member session to retrieve. Must be a valid UUID representing an existing session record.
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Update the global profile information of the currently authenticated member.

This operation allows members to modify their personal profile information that is shared across all organizations they belong to. The profile includes the display name shown throughout the interface, an optional avatar image for visual identification, and an optional phone number for contact purposes.

Members have exclusive rights to modify their own global profile. No other user, including organization owners or administrators, can modify another user's global profile. Profile modifications take effect immediately across all organization contexts where the user is a member.

The display name appears in place of the email address throughout the system, providing a more personalized experience. Avatar images provide visual identification, while phone numbers serve as supplementary contact information. All profile fields are optional and can be added, modified, or removed at any time.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update the erp_hrm_members record for the currently authenticated user. Validate that displayName (if provided) is a non-empty string. Validate that phoneNumber (if provided) follows acceptable phone number format. Handle avatar image update through file upload URL reference if changed. Update only the fields provided in the request body - partial updates are allowed. Ensure member is authenticated and has an active session before processing. Return the complete updated member profile with all global profile fields.

responseBody.description: Updated member profile with global profile information

requestBody.description: Profile update data with optional displayName, avatar, and phoneNumber fields

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organizations accessible to the current user.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for organizations including partial name matching, currency filtering, timezone filtering, and creation date ranges. It supports the multi-organization membership model where users can belong to multiple organizations simultaneously.

The response includes organization summary information optimized for list displays, showing key identity and configuration fields (name, description, logo, currency, timezone, fiscal settings) without exposing full detailed data.

Results are scoped to organizations the authenticated user has access to - either organizations they own or organizations where they have an active membership. Data isolation between organizations is strictly enforced at the API level.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options. Use this endpoint to populate organization selection interfaces, dashboard overviews, and administrative organization management screens.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_organizations table with pagination and filtering support.

Filter capabilities:
- name: partial text search on organization name
- ownerId: filter by organization owner
- currency: filter by ISO 4217 currency code
- timezone: filter by IANA timezone
- createdAt range: filter by creation date
- Include deleted organizations option (for admin/owner recovery scenarios)

Join with erp_hrm_members to include owner information in response.

Authorization:
- Members can only view organizations they belong to (via erp_hrm_organization_members)
- Organization owners can view their owned organizations
- System administrators may view all organizations

Sorting options:
- createdAt (default, descending)
- name (alphabetical)
- updatedAt

Pagination:
- Cursor-based pagination for large result sets
- Configurable page size (default 20, max 100)

Returns summary fields: id, name, description, logoUrl, currency, timezone, fiscalYearStartMonth, createdAt, owner summary.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering organizations

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific organization by its ID.

This operation returns complete organization details including identity information (name, description, logo) and configuration settings (currency, timezone, fiscal year start month). It serves the organization context selection workflow where members view available organizations and their details before selecting one to work in.

Members can only retrieve organizations they are members of. The returned data includes the organization owner's ID for reference. Configuration fields like currency, timezone, and fiscal_year_start_month are essential for displaying organization settings in the UI.

Related operations include PATCH /organizations for listing user's organizations with filtering, and PUT /organizations/{organizationId} for updating organization settings (requires appropriate permissions).
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_organizations table by id field using the provided organizationId path parameter.

1. Verify the organization exists and deleted_at is null (not soft-deleted)
2. Verify the requesting user has membership in the target organization (check erp_hrm_organization_members where organization_id matches and user_id matches the authenticated user)
3. Return the full organization record including all columns

Join with erp_hrm_members table to include owner information if needed for display purposes.

Authorization: Only members of the organization can view its details. Non-members receive 403 Forbidden.

responseBody.description: Complete organization details with configuration settings

operations.description:
Create a new organization in the erpHrm system.

This operation establishes a new tenant organization that serves as the aggregate root for all organization-scoped data isolation. The authenticated user becomes the organization owner and is granted full administrative privileges.

Upon creation, the system initializes the organization with the provided identity information (name, description, optional logo URL) and operational configuration (currency in ISO 4217 format, IANA timezone identifier, and fiscal year starting month). The organization's deleted_at field remains null indicating active status.

The created organization automatically links to the authenticated user via owner_id. All subsequent entities (departments, roles, projects, members, etc.) will belong to this organization and remain isolated from other organizations.

Multi-tenancy is enforced at the database level through organization_id foreign keys across all related entities. The new organization is immediately available for member invitations and operational use.

Returns the complete organization record including server-generated id and timestamps.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Extract authenticated user ID from JWT session token
2. Validate required fields from IErpHrmOrganization.ICreate:
   - name: non-empty string, unique across all organizations (check @@unique constraint)
   - currency: ISO 4217 format (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'KRW')
   - timezone: valid IANA timezone string (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Asia/Seoul')
   - fiscal_year_start_month: integer 1-12 representing month
   - description: optional string
   - logo_url: optional URL string, validate format

3. Check for duplicate organization name violation against erp_hrm_organizations table
4. Generate UUID for new organization id
5. Set timestamps: created_at = updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
6. Set owner_id to authenticated user ID
7. Set deleted_at = null
8. Insert record into erp_hrm_organizations table
9. Return complete IErpHrmOrganization DTO

Database operations:
- INSERT INTO erp_hrm_organizations (id, owner_id, name, description, logo_url, currency, timezone, fiscal_year_start_month, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)
- SELECT to verify unique name constraint before insert

Error handling:
- Duplicate name: return 409 Conflict
- Invalid currency format: return 400 Bad Request
- Invalid timezone: return 400 Bad Request
- Invalid fiscal_year_start_month (not 1-12): return 400 Bad Request
- Unauthenticated: return 401 Unauthorized

responseBody.description: Created organization with all fields

requestBody.description: Organization creation data including name, description, logo, currency, timezone, and fiscal year settings

operations.description:
Update an existing organization's details and settings.

This operation allows authorized members to modify organization attributes such as name, description, and configuration settings. The organization serves as the root container for all business data within the platform, including employees, departments, projects, and roles.

The operation requires the caller to have appropriate permissions within the organization context. Upon successful update, the system returns the complete updated organization record with all current field values. The organization identity and its relationships to child entities remain intact during the update process.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement organization update by querying erp_hrm_organizations table using provided organizationId UUID.
Validate that the caller has organization:update permission.
Update only provided fields in the request body (partial update support).
Common updatable fields include name, description, settings, configuration.
Return the complete updated organization record joined with related owner information if applicable.
Handle edge cases: non-existent organization (404), insufficient permissions (403), duplicate organization names if uniqueness constraint exists (409).

operations.description:
Delete an organization permanently from the platform.

This operation permanently removes an organization and all its associated data from the system. Deletion is subject to strict business constraints to ensure data integrity and proper business closure procedures.

Before deletion, the system validates that there are no pending timesheets awaiting approval or rejection, and that there are no active employee contracts remaining. These checks ensure proper business closure procedures before an organization is dissolved.

When deletion is permitted, the operation performs a CASCADE DELETE that permanently removes all associated data including:
- All employee records and their memberships
- All departments and hierarchies
- All projects, tasks, and project memberships
- All timelogs, timesheets, and activity logs
- All roles and contracts

The organization owner's user account is preserved but disassociated from the deleted organization. This deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Implementation must verify the requesting user is the organization owner before allowing deletion. Query erp_hrm_timesheets table to check for pending status timesheets - if any exist, reject with error indicating pending timesheets must be resolved first. Query erp_hrm_contracts table to check for is_active = true records - if any exist, reject with error indicating active contracts must be terminated first. If validation passes, perform soft delete by setting deleted_at = current_timestamp on the organization record. Cascade the soft delete to all child entities: erp_hrm_organization_members (cascade), erp_hrm_roles (cascade), erp_hrm_departments (cascade), erp_hrm_projects (cascade), erp_hrm_tasks (cascade), erp_hrm_timelogs (cascade), erp_hrm_timesheets (cascade). Preserve owner user account but remove organization association. Return the soft-deleted organization record including the deleted_at timestamp.

prerequisites.description: Organization must exist before it can be deleted. The organizationId path parameter references an Organization entity that must be created first via POST /erpHrm/member/organizations.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organization members (employees) belonging to the currently selected organization.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for employee management. Members can be filtered by activation status (active/deactivated), department assignment, assigned role, employment type (full_time, part_time, contractor, intern), and position/title.

The response includes member summary information containing the membership details along with linked user profile information (display name, email, avatar) and role information for proper identification. This endpoint is essential for employee directory browsing, management dashboards, and organizational reporting.

Organization context is determined by the current session's selected organization. All returned members belong to this organization context. Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient navigation through large employee lists.

Permission-based access: Users with employee management permission (employee:manage) can view all members including deactivated ones. Regular members can view active colleagues based on their role permissions.

Soft-deleted members (where deleted_at is not null) are excluded from results to maintain clean employee lists while preserving historical records.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_organization_members table with organization scoping from session context.

Join with erp_hrm_members for user profile data (first_name, last_name, email, avatar_url).
Join with erp_hrm_roles for role name and description.
Join with erp_hrm_departments for department name (if department_id exists).

Apply filters from request body:
- is_active: Filter by activation status (true/false/null for all)
- department_id: Filter by specific department, array for multiple, null for no department assignment
- role_id: Filter by assigned role
- employment_type: Filter by employment classification (full_time, part_time, contractor, intern)
- position: Partial text search on position field (case-insensitive, uses GIN index)
- user_id: Filter by specific user (for checking existing membership)

Add WHERE organization_id = current_organization_id from session.
Exclude records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

Pagination:
- cursor-based with created_at as tie-breaker
- page_size from request (default 20, max 100)
- Return pagination object with next_cursor, prev_cursor, total_count

Sorting:
- Default sort by created_at DESC (newest first)
- Support position, department name, role name sorts

Response structure:
- data: Array of IErpHrmOrganizationMember.ISummary
- pagination: Cursor-based pagination metadata

Each summary includes:
- id, organization_id, role_id, department_id
- employment_type, position, is_active
- user: Embedded user info (id, email, first_name, last_name, avatar_url)
- role: Embedded role name
- department: Embedded department name (if exists)
- created_at, updated_at

Edge cases:
- Empty department_id shows members without department assignment
- Deactivated members returned only if is_active filter explicitly false
- Position search uses trigram similarity for fuzzy matching
